acts.desc:
Host Ira Glass goes to Tijuana, Mexico where people trying to come to the U.S. asking for asylum have devised a new way to keep track of their place in line.
Cindy Carcamo first wrote about this story for the Los Angeles Times.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Reporter Julia Preston goes to a mass hearing in McAllen, Texas where 74 immigrants are being charged in a federal courtroom as a result of zero tolerance. Julia is a contributing writer for The Marshall Project, which published a print version of this story.
acts.title: All Together Now

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: All the little and not-so-little ways the Trump administration is tightening its scrutiny of immigrants.
acts.title: Kitchen Sink

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: A bunch of government emails recently came out as part of a class-action lawsuit. The emails show new appointees trying to roll back one particular part of immigration policy that could result in half a million people having to leave the United States. Producer Nadia Reiman takes us inside the world of these emails.
acts.title: The Terminators

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: The President has cut the number of refugees officially allowed into the U.S. So a bunch of refugee resettlement offices are shutting down. Producer Zoe Chace goes to one of these offices that’s about to close.
acts.title: Now IRC Me, Now You Don’t

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Refugee resettlement policy changed dramatically from the first week President Trump took office. In that first travel ban, the president halted the entire refugee resettlement program, until we could, in his words from the campaign, "Figure out what the hell is going on." Producer Zoe Chace has the story of the group tasked to figure out what the hell was going on, and why the number of refugees resettling is the lowest in the history of the program.
acts.title: Why So Few
